paper.title_en: Constraining curvature and anisotropy in wCDM and ΛCDM cosmologies
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we present observational constraints on the simplest isotropic and anisotropic extensions of the standard dark-energy cosmologies using a comprehensive combination of datasets, including Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), Cosmic Chronometers (CC), the Pantheon Plus (PP) compilation of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), and SH0ES Cepheid host-galaxy distance anchors. In all analyses, the upper bounds on the anisotropy parameter are constrained to be of the order of <math altimg="si58.svg"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup></math> at 95% CL. For the data combination including SH0ES calibration, the inferred values of the Hubble constant are <math altimg="si59.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>72.4</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mspace width="0.33em"/><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">km</mi><mspace width="0.33em"/><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.33em"/><msup><mtext>Mpc</mtext><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></math> for all models, at the 68% CL. The constraints on the curvature density parameter Ωκ0 are consistent with zero at 68% CL in all models from both data combinations, providing no statistically significant evidence for a departure from spatial flatness, <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msub><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Ω</mi></mstyle><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Furthermore, we perform a statistical model comparison using the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria to assess the relative performance of the models with the observational datasets.
